answers.answer: There are 12 ordinary turns per player (four seasons × three ordinary rounds). Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; courtship is ‘an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Rotate Quarters servants to Available, then Expended servants to Quarters; resolve the round event, then ongoing monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity; play exactly the required gentry; assign required service; resolve positive favours before negative; optionally buy; cleanup sends used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and the tile back to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hosting: ordered steps 1–8 and end-of-turn round check.

answers.answer: Pass in this order: servants directly to Available; discard gentry to hand; event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Passing has no activity favours and does not flip a tile. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.’

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, before special actions; level 6 satisfies PR6. Four Service Help actions cost 12 increments, moving servants from Quarters to Available, and may lower actual reputation to 3.4 without invalidating the tile or guests. Both tile and guests use the level at the end of step 2 for screening.
answers.evidence: Reputation section: ‘Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2’; later changes do not invalidate play. Service Help costs 3 increments per servant.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; otherwise choose their order. At minimum you cannot avoid a negative reputation loss by taking it first; losses stop at 1.1. A guest with a money penalty can be played only if the full payment is payable; use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money, and if still unfunded you cannot play it.
answers.evidence: Hosting: ‘positive favours before all negative favours’; Money section: ‘You cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation’ and money penalty must be fully payable.

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments to move one servant from Quarters to Available, repeatable; it cannot take one directly from Expended. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments for a full Market refresh, once per turn. Special actions require reputation to pay and cannot be used at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum-reputation rule.

answers.answer: Host the base Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry; take up to two non-underbutler servants from Servants for Hire into Expended Service, without a hiring fee. The tile upgrades on first use. Its upgraded side instead lets you recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s board into your Expended Service; no unique servant can be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Room entry.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, footmen may substitute for valets only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant even while that regular servant remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; it goes immediately into Expended Service. Butler’s Room and Hire Servant VP cards cannot hire it. It is unique and cannot be recruited by another player.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Pantry and underbutler rules.

answers.answer: Market price is the space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot fall below £100. You may not acquire a duplicate you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchase; PR limits play, not acquisition.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: purchase price and duplicate rules; reputation section on acquiring above reputation.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. Stack duplicates on their matching Market tile and draw again; duplicates share one space/price. Reserve-eligible draws go straight to Reserve and are replaced. If you buy only one tile from a duplicate stack, the space remains occupied and there is no refill. When filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar; later Service draws go directly to Reserve except that tile. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and send later PR1 draws there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh sections; Overview confirms full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At courtships 1–3 return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall, total tile VP in the current face-up theme category (including negative VP; only the visible hybrid category counts). Highest scorer gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild; tied leaders each draw a VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one objective, simultaneous discards shuffled together to the deck bottom. Then move Reserve tiles, refresh Market, reveal the next theme to the right of prior themes, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep, steps 1–4 and post-courtship order.

answers.answer: Final courtship totals tile VP across all four revealed themes, with categories counted once per appearance, including negative VP; highest gets a VP card and Fairchild. A tie is broken by reputation level (wheel position ignored); if still tied no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP-card benefits before Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship paragraph.

answers.answer: End-game VP comes from face-up tile VP (including negatives), gentry in hand and discard (including negatives/family/final Fairchild), fulfilled objectives, reputation level (1–7 scores 1/3/6/10/15/21/28), 2 VP per servant of any type/location, £1 VP per £200 rounded down, and retained VP cards. Ties: final Fairchild, then highest reputation level, then shared victory. Wealth position and reputation wheel position do not break ties.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup plus two on round 6, then discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three. Extra objectives from Main Library or VP cards increase the retained final count and do not cause an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down at the objective deck bottom. Tile objectives require ownership at game end, not upgrade status.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards opening paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, any time on your later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it for its printed benefit; used cards go to the VP deck bottom. Retained unused cards stay hidden and score their printed VP. You cannot receive both benefit and VP from one card.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP card rules.

answers.answer: Normal activity tiles must flip to their rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded. Ongoing-only tiles cannot host or upgrade. Hybrids start with underlined icon up, flip after every use, and move to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) gets one activity use, then becomes a monument and cannot host again; benefit starts on later turns. Courtship/objective category for hybrids is the currently face-up icon.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal, hybrids, monuments.

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve in the ongoing-effects step on hosting and passing turns, after round event; monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn but not during courtship or on the purchase turn. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant to reduce one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; servant goes to Expended at turn end and cannot also serve the activity. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: monuments and Servants’ Hall.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: footman on tile plus one casual guest from hand with normal guest service; doubles all favours, including negative; upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile plus one prestige guest from hand with normal guest service; doubles one chosen favour; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draws one prestige guest to attend with no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours only, keeps guest in discard at cleanup, then upgrades into a monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and fixed-count sentence.

answers.answer: Randomly give the first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose available base family boards. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Set common reputation baseline to level 1, position 1; after family bonus Cavendish starts 1.4 and Asquith, Ponsonby, York 1.1. Use counters 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max with 1 showing (no 7/8 counters). Each player gets butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter side showing; Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady. Ponsonby is the only family starting with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire has three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game; they cannot later be hired.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers/housekeepers; boxed servants unavailable.

answers.answer: Shuffle starter guests separately from casual guests and deal two to each player; shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow ordinary casual rules, not a separate in-game guest type.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry section: starter guests are casual guests.

answers.answer: Four-player setup selects five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). You may select at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Put selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles in the bag; tiles that later upgrade into monuments remain in the bag and do not count against the selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Fill six different spaces with eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set aside ineligible draws and return them after filling; stack duplicates in the same space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending sorting number from £300 space. PR4, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments cannot enter.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme for open courtship and keep revealed themes in order. Put base Charles and Elizabeth face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is public, not hidden; old revealed themes remain in order/play for final courtship.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Final courtship totals across all four revealed themes.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available first; the servant in Expended then moves to Quarters. An available servant you do not use remains Available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: Quarters to Available then Expended to Quarters; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: If Private Study is not upgraded at the event check, you get no Village Fair reward then; you may host it later that turn but that does not retroactively earn the reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on standard Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track table: Village Fair at 3 and 9, reward only if Study already upgraded at that step.

answers.answer: Round 6 event is resolved before ongoing tile effects, after service rotation on hosting turns or after servant/gentry recovery on passes. Draw two objectives and keep both secret. The event applies to each player’s turn, including passing players.
answers.evidence: Round-track events section: event timing; table says space 6 Draw Objectives: draw two, keep both.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. All other requirements still apply, including exact gentry counts/types and service.
answers.evidence: Round-track table, space 14.

answers.answer: Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds. Make all purchases from the unchanged market at prices applying before the sequence; do not slide/refill until finished and do not refresh between purchases. Market Purchase VP cards use the same purchase rules and restrictions.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while refilling all six spaces under normal rules. They cannot reappear in that refresh; return them to the bag and mix only after replacements are drawn. Reserve remains unchanged.
answers.evidence: Refresh paragraph: set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged, refill, then return set-aside tiles to bag.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment; clockwise gains, anticlockwise losses. Passing wheel position 5 to 1 raises a level; passing 1 to 5 lowers one. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond minimum. To avoid wasting gains at maximum, spend excess immediately on special actions, including before or during a reputation favour to make space.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions section.

answers.answer: Money is public. Players cannot give or receive money from one another in this mode. Costs cannot exceed holdings. The common supply is unlimited; use proxies if necessary.
answers.evidence: Money paragraph.

answers.answer: For two ladies, any two female family members or female guests qualify. For two casual guests, family cannot qualify; the attendees must be casual guests. Play the exact required count, never extra. Family needs no personal service and has no PR, while guests/tile must satisfy screening at the level fixed after step 2.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4: exact requirements and Ladies definition; reputation section: family no PR/no personal service.

answers.answer: Ordinary invite favours draw the indicated guest from its deck, reveal it to everyone, and add it to hand. Screening draws the stated number, chooses the stated number to keep, reveals only kept cards and adds them to hand; rejected cards go unseen to the bottom of their deck.
answers.evidence: Gentry invite procedure table and screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one just drawn by an earlier favour. Family cannot be dismissed. Put dismissed guests on the bottom of their matching guest deck; they are no longer yours, do not return on passing, and score no VP.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest (choice). Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Thus Lady and Heir offer choices; Lord and Dowager give stated benefit(s), and Dowager gives both.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: The admirer bonus triggers with Charles Fairchild or another male prestige guest, not with a male casual guest or female prestige guest. Bonus is two reputation. Young Lady still draws one casual guest in every case.
answers.evidence: Family card table says draw one casual; additional two reputation if male prestige attends; Charles is male prestige and triggers it.

answers.answer: Charles is a prestige guest, no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a prestige guest, no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives one prestige guest plus two reputation. Both are guests, not family, so neither has family dismissal immunity and either may be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: Fairchild sex/type/service/VP and dismissal; Fairchild favour sentence.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and costs you one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by either reduction.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: base gossips; minimum-reputation protection.

answers.answer: A Barn grants one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Mere ownership of an Estate tile and passing do not earn it.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Barn.

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then Expended to Quarters. The Servants’ Quarters improvement additionally lets you use one servant still in Quarters directly, with no reputation cost; it goes to Expended at turn end. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments and moves one Quarters servant to Available (not directly from Expended), repeatably.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Servants’ Quarters tile and service mechanism table.

answers.answer: Front Private Study requires one butler and exactly two family members, with no tile favour; it upgrades permanently after use. Once upgraded it is an ongoing tile, not an activity, and on Village Fair rounds 3 and 9 yields £300 and two reputation without staffing or hosting it again.
answers.evidence: Improvements: Private Study; Village Fair table.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library uses one butler and two family, and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library uses one butler and three family, and draws one VP card. The extra objective increases the retained objective count for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Improvements: Main Library.

answers.answer: Objective VP benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other face down to the bottom of the objective deck. The kept card is one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: Objective benefit.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants, including Expended servants, directly to Available and makes them usable immediately. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Service.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire into Expended Service; underbutler is excluded. It cannot provide service immediately from Expended (unless later moved through a permitted mechanism).
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Hire Servant; Expended location and service rules.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest returns one gentry, including a family member, from your personal discard to your hand. Used before attendee selection, you may then play that card as an attendee this activity if it meets requirements; returning to hand alone does not make it attend.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service VP counts every servant type, 2 VP each; the ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: basic-servant note and servant objective table; Final VP: servants.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite is both a monument and an Estate tile; upgraded Lionheart Suite is both a monument and a Prestige tile. They count for their category objective and the monument objective. Hybrids count only in their currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference opening paragraph.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus Main Library or North Library. Owning the listed tiles at game end suffices; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: group objectives and ownership rule.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest. Every-three-guests objective scores 1 VP per complete set of three nonfamily guests; an incomplete group scores nothing. The final Fairchild is a prestige guest and counts; family does not count as guests for these objectives.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: ‘Guest excludes family; prestige guests include a final Fairchild’; guest bonuses table.

answers.answer: Reputation objective gives 7 VP for maximum level 7 regardless of wheel position. Wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP or reputation tie resolution; reputation scoring uses level, and wheel position never breaks a tie.
answers.evidence: Base objective table; Final VP table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Both sides require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded West Terrace draws one prestige guest. Upgraded West Terrace draws one prestige guest and may dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottoms of their matching decks. It remains an activity tile, not an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements: West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no maximum hand or personal-discard size. Guests in the discard pile still belong to you and score normally; passing recovers them to hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry section opening sentence.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-only rule. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You are not required to host whenever able; you may choose to pass. If your preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Hosting steps 4–5; Passing section offers passing choice.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may use the free pass refresh, one paid special-action refresh, and multiple Market Refresh VP cards. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action Refresh Market; pass refreshes and VP-card refreshes are separate methods. If using a Builders’ Holiday or Market Purchase sequence, however, no refresh may occur between purchases.
answers.evidence: Special actions paragraph and Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase restrictions.

answers.answer: No interrupt actions are allowed while another player takes a turn. Special actions may be taken any time on your own turn, hosting or passing, with sufficient reputation; VP cards may be used at any time on your own later turn. The summary does not separately state interrupt timing for each listed action, but own-turn timing covers them.
answers.evidence: Special actions: ‘available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing’; VP cards: ‘at any time on your own later turn.’

answers.answer: No. Favour benefits are mandatory unless expressly optional, so a printed ordinary guest invite must be resolved while enjoying other favours. An optional dismissal is different: it may be declined, and if taken requires selecting an eligible guest to dismiss.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: favours mandatory unless expressly optional; Gentry section: dismissal always optional.
